Adolescents with congenital hypothyroidism and typically developing adolescents. No adult group.
Temporal lobe resection patients during memory encoding. Encoding and patient focused.
Review of a single lesion case. No primary group retrieval contrast.
Social context during encoding, with recognition after scanning. Encoding only.
Prospective memory with working memory updating. Not episodic retrieval success.
Children and adults, N = 126, with correct source vs incorrect source vs miss at retrieval. The adult group fits, but the analysis is hippocampal, so whole-brain reporting decides this.
ALE meta-analysis of incidental memory. Not primary data.
Review of autobiographical memory in depression. Not primary data.
Subliminal face-occupation pairs facilitating retrieval of celebrity occupations. Mainly semantic and congruency effects, not remembered vs forgotten.
Prospective memory in young and older adults. Not episodic retrieval success.
Cortisol during sleep, with remote vs recent items in scanned recognition. Compares consolidation status and drug, not a success contrast.
Single case with superior memory, using structural and resting-state imaging. No task contrast.
Event-related potentials in early AD and controls. No fMRI or PET activation.
Discourse comprehension and consistency judgments. Not an episodic retrieval task.
Repeated autobiographical retrieval with shifts in content focus. No failed-retrieval contrast.
PREVENT-AD precuneus activity during successful retrieval, related to amyloid and APOE. A regional biomarker analysis in the cohort of pmid:32474466, not a separate success map.
Delayed match-to-sample working memory with subsequent memory testing. Working memory and encoding.
Default mode activity during encoding related to resting amplitude. Encoding only.

Children and adults in associative recognition, with recognized vs forgotten discrimination in the hippocampus. Adults may qualify, but the analysis is hippocampal, so whole-brain reporting decides this.
Event boundaries at encoding and later temporal estimates. Encoding only.
PREVENT-AD sex differences using PLS during encoding and item retrieval. Same cohort as pmid:32474466, with no separate retrieval-success table described.

Schizophrenia patients and 16 controls in old/new word recognition, with correct responses analysed. Controls could provide old vs new if tabled separately, but results are framed as group differences.
Memory conformity under social pressure with genotype. Not remembered vs forgotten.
PTSD therapy and brain state dynamics during picture viewing. No memory retrieval contrast.
Covert verbal fluency tasks. Semantic and language retrieval, not episodic.
Decoding encoding, retrieval and integration states during learning. Classifier study without a retrieval-success map.
Awake human infants with subsequent memory. Not adults, and encoding.

Young and older adults comparing failed with successful retrieval across autobiographical, episodic and semantic tasks. The episodic task gives a success contrast, reported mainly in the failed > successful direction; check the opposite direction.
Resting-state connectivity in music students. No memory task.
Saccade-based grid codes during scene study, predicting later memory. Encoding only.
Creative idea generation vs recall of old ideas. Creativity study with no retrieval-success contrast.
Reactivation during a museum tour paradigm, analysed by subsequent true and false memory. Encoding-like analysis.
Seed connectivity of DLPFC and hippocampus across adult life span during context memory. Connectivity rather than a source-correct activation table.
Factual knowledge recall in surgical patients. Semantic and patient-only.
aMCI and controls with structural MRI and FDG-PET related to behavioural scores. No task activation.
Amyloid PET and structural MRI related to memory stages. PET measures pathology, with no task contrast.
Single brain-injury case with a misidentification delusion. No group imaging contrast.
Working memory decoding in younger and older adults. Explicit exclusion.
Feature reactivation in people with deficient autobiographical memory and comparison participants. Reactivation measures rather than a retrieval-success map.
Hippocampal representations during repeated associative learning. Encoding and learning analysis.
Object naming in older adults by APOE genotype. Semantic word retrieval, not episodic.

Young and older adults in scanned retrieval, with successful novelty for related and unrelated lures. The focus is correct rejection processes; check whether hits vs correct rejections are also tabled.
Past and future event clusters. Autobiographical organization with no failed-retrieval contrast.
Reinstatement patterns for sounds and videos. Pattern analysis, not retrieval success.
Scalp EEG markers of recollection. No fMRI or PET.
Sleeping two-year-olds in fMRI. Not adults and not a retrieval task.
Yohimbine or placebo, with recognition scanned 1 or 28 days after encoding. The placebo group may give a success contrast, but reported effects concern drug and delay.
Speech registration in memory-impaired patients and controls. Attention and encoding, not episodic retrieval.
Intracranial recordings in three patients. No fMRI or PET contrast of retrieval success.
Think/no-think suppression of autobiographical memories. Suppression, not retrieval success.
Time-based prospective memory. Not episodic retrieval success.
Attention and subsequent source memory during encoding. Encoding only.
Review of the hippocampus in unconscious memory. No primary data.
Working memory fMRI in aMCI and controls related to outside-scanner tests. Working memory exclusion.
Viewing safe-sex ads, with recall afterward. Encoding-like and persuasion focused.
Cerebellar volume in patients. Structural only.
Non-conscious visual sequence learning in V1, explicitly without conscious retrieval. Not episodic retrieval success.
Dynamic connectivity in schizophrenia and controls. No activation contrast.
Sentence novelty during comprehension, with recognition later. Encoding and novelty processing.
Late-onset depression vs controls in a face-name task. Group differences only, with a small control group and no stated success contrast.
Short-delay match-to-sample with respiratory timing. Working memory style task.
FDG-PET in transient global amnesia. Resting metabolism in patients.
Temporal context retrieval with stimulus and response load, compared with an ordering task. Task and load effects rather than correct vs incorrect.
Behavioural retrieval-induced forgetting experiments. No imaging.
BDNF genotype in 58 healthy adults during encoding and retrieval. Genotype correlation, with no retrieval-success table stated.
EEG classification in a think/no-think paradigm. No fMRI or PET.
EEG during autobiographical retrieval. No fMRI or PET.
Episodic reinstatement intruding on working memory. Working memory paradigm with pattern analysis.
Portable fNIRS during real-world prospective memory. Not fMRI or PET, nor episodic retrieval success.
ERP study of masked priming and recognition. No fMRI or PET.
Valence learning for pseudowords, with amygdala responses by anxiety. Emotional learning rather than retrieval success.
Autobiographical memories of different ages with SVM classification. No failed-retrieval contrast.
Generalized PPI of hippocampal connectivity by APOE genotype. Connectivity, not retrieval-success activation.

Picture naming practice. Language, not episodic retrieval success.

Prestimulus hippocampal activity at study predicting later recollection. Encoding only.
Resting-state connectivity from meta-analytic seeds. No task contrast.

Resting-state connectivity related to interview scores. No task retrieval contrast.
Selectivity during item and associative encoding, with recognition outside the scanner. Encoding only.
Emotional association encoding with later memory test. Encoding only.
Posthypnotic amnesia and memory suppression during scanned tests. Compares suggestion conditions, not remembered vs forgotten.

Arousal and reward anticipation during memory formation. Encoding only.
Review of hippocampal activation in PTSD. No primary data.
Neural selectivity during learning in older adults. Encoding only.
Decoding of spatial content across working and long-term memory. Representational format, not retrieval success.
Temporal lobe epilepsy patients, with lateralization of activation. Patient-only.

26 healthy adults remembering whether an item was a picture or a word, with analysis of errors. Reality monitoring is a source judgment; check whether correct vs incorrect source is reported rather than only imagery groups.
Depressed patients and 23 controls, with recognition during retrieval. Controls might give a success contrast, but results are group differences and encoding relationships.
Hippocampal subfield volumes related to memory scores. Structural only.
Oxytocin during trait judgments, with recall afterward. Encoding and self-processing.

True vs false context memory with shapes, using conjunctions of confident responses. Effectively hits vs false alarms, which the criteria exclude, though a source-correct check is possible.
Spaced learning and repetition suppression during encoding. Encoding only.
Angular gyrus connectivity during rest and silent autobiographical retrieval. No success contrast.
Borderline personality patients recalling life events over a year. Patient-only.
Children during scene encoding and rest. Children and encoding.
Viewing social interactions in a movie. Not a memory task.
Breast cancer patients and controls in a verbal recall task. Group differences during retrieval, with no stated correct vs failed contrast in controls.
ALE meta-analysis of false memory. Not primary data.
Healthy young adults with resting connectivity, but also task-evoked activation during successful retrieval. Object-location retrieval may give a success contrast; check for a table of it.
Background connectivity distinguishing perception from retrieval states. No retrieval-success contrast.
TMS effects on episodic details. Behavioural, with no retrieval-success activation.
Single case of developmental amnesia with MVPA. Pattern analysis focused on a patient.
CACNA1C genotype effects during encoding and retrieval in two healthy samples. Genotype contrast, with no retrieval-success table stated.
Prospective memory in postpartum women. Not episodic retrieval success.
Rat microPET during fear memory recall. Not human.
Multiple sclerosis and controls, with encoding of correctly remembered items reported. Patient comparison, focused on encoding.
Resting-state connectivity related to autobiographical details. No task retrieval.
Epilepsy patients and controls in autobiographical recall. No failed-retrieval contrast.
Negative subsequent memory at encoding in older and young adults. Encoding only.
Lesion patients with parietal damage. Behavioural, with no functional imaging contrast.
TMS in older adults, with fMRI signals for recollection memory formation. Encoding-related measures within a targeted network and a stimulation focus.
Classifier method for decoding semantic categories. Methods paper.

Children and adults (18 to 25) recalling which colour was paired with each drawing, with correct recall indexing retrieval. The adult group fits, and cortical as well as hippocampal effects are reported.
Subsequent memory for imagined future events. Encoding of simulations.
Past and future event generation in depression and controls. No failed-retrieval contrast.
Emotional word pairs retrieved three weeks later, with reinstatement focus. RSA and encoding analysis, though a retrieval success contrast may be incidental.
Nicotine and prospective memory. Not episodic retrieval success.
Developmental amnesia patients and controls, with scene reinstatement effects. Reinstatement by encoding context rather than retrieval success.
Verbal joke comprehension. Not a memory task.
Same memory palace work as pmid:39651289, with room reliability predicting reinstatement. Representation study.
APOE genotype in healthy young adults during encoding and retrieval. Genotype differences, with no stated retrieval-success table.
Adolescents and young adults with ASD or typical development, with encoding focus. Not an adult retrieval-success analysis.
CA3 lesion patients with resting-state 7T. No task retrieval contrast.
Single individual with superior memory at rest. No task contrast.
Meta-analysis of space and time in episodic memory. Not primary data.
Single case with bilateral hippocampal damage. Not a healthy group.
Learned event sequences with internal or external perspective. Distance effects, not retrieval success.
Value-based encoding of words. Encoding only.
Older adults with stable or declining memory, with functional change across four years. Longitudinal group differences, with no stated retrieval-success contrast.
Meta-analysis of paired associate recollection. Not primary data, but its Hit > Miss studies can be cross-checked.
Review of infant memory development. Not primary data.
Older adults with encoding and retrieval vs control trials, related to carotenoid levels. Task vs control and a nutrition correlate.
Former football players by concussion history during relational retrieval. Group and exposure comparison, not a clear healthy-group success contrast.
Prestimulus activity predicts subsequent memory. Encoding only.
Bed rest and exercise intervention, with encoding and retrieval activity by group. No retrieval-success contrast.
True and false associative memories, with hits and correct rejections compared in the analyses. False-memory contrasts are not eligible, but associative hits vs correct rejections look available.

Selective retrieval vs re-exposure, and retrieval-induced forgetting. Retrieval practice vs relearning, not correct vs failed retrieval.

Published version of pmid:40463131 on event boundaries and time dilation. Encoding only.
aMCI vs controls across three paradigms. A pilot on paradigm efficiency without a stated success contrast.
Two dissociative amnesia cases. Not a healthy group.
Near-death memories in a block recall vs rest design. Retrieval vs rest only.
Emotion suppression during successful encoding. Encoding only.
Spatial memory for shapes at retrieval, with left hits vs left misses producing hippocampal effects. Source-correct vs incorrect fits, so check for whole-brain coverage and both visual fields.
Encoding instructions and subsequent memory. Encoding only.
ERP study in schizophrenia and controls. No fMRI or PET.
Cortisol during recognition and room recall in a virtual apartment, focused on semantic substitution. Addresses memory errors rather than successful retrieval.
Recognition with strong and weak lists in rapid event-related fMRI, with effects on foils and angular gyrus. Old vs new may be tabled, but the focus is foils across list strength.
Resting MEG in patients with memory impairment. Not task fMRI or PET.
Plasma biomarkers in a memory clinic. No retrieval imaging.
Adolescents with obesity during encoding. Not adults, and encoding.

Never-depressed twins at high and low familial risk, with word recognition during fMRI and retrieval-specific activity. Whole-sample contrasts may exist, but emotional-word and risk comparisons are the focus.

Self-reflection on past and present in autism. Not a retrieval-success contrast.

Working memory suppression and later associative learning. Maintenance and encoding effects with MVPA.

Bipolar, schizophrenia and 14 controls in an emotional memory paradigm. Reported effects are viewing and group differences, with no retrieval-success table stated.
Encoding-related activity in transient epileptic amnesia. Encoding only.
Implicit contingency learning, with retrieval compared to a non-memory matching baseline. The abstract states it did not contrast successful with unsuccessful performance.
Schizophrenia and controls, contrasting source recognition with object recognition. A task comparison, not source-correct vs incorrect.
Reboxetine during autobiographical recall. Drug and valence, with no failed-retrieval contrast.

Hydrocortisone during autobiographical retrieval. No failed-retrieval contrast.

Cued recall by intentional or incidental test, contrasting studied with unstudied cues when the target was produced. A retrieval-success contrast in healthy adults; use the intentional group.
30 younger adults with targets and related lures at retrieval. False-memory contrasts are not eligible, but target hits vs correct rejections may exist; check tables.

Replication of pattern similarity during encoding. Subsequent memory analysis.

Semantic processing during encoding, with recognition afterwards. Encoding only.
Review of hippocampus and serial order. Not primary data.

Collective schema and recall of museum displays in mPFC. Memory organization, not retrieval success.

Children with febrile seizures and control children. Not adults.
Route and survey navigation learned over days. Spatial retrieval without failed-retrieval contrast.

Picture-word interference. Language production, not episodic retrieval.

tDCS in early Alzheimer's disease with fMRI and MEG. Patient-only.

Depressed and control participants recognizing old narrative items vs new ones. Successful identification is reported, but stimuli are personal narratives; check for a control-group old vs new table.

DCM of scene construction, imagination and autobiographical retrieval. No retrieval-success contrast.
Intracranial EEG in the default mode network. No fMRI or PET.

24 healthy adults in old-new recognition with confidence, comparing forgotten and correctly rejected items. Hits vs correct rejections may also be tabled, but this paper emphasizes nonconscious memory.
TMS and connectivity during autobiographical retrieval vs rest. No success contrast.
Hippocampal attentional state during encoding. Encoding only.
Survivors of partner violence and controls in verbal recognition during fMRI. Control group may give an old vs new table, but the abstract reports only group differences.
Reading emotional adjectives, with surprise recall afterward. Not a retrieval analysis.

Normal participants, MCI and AD during free recall of heard sentences, with activity by recall accuracy. Normal participants may give a recalled vs reduced recall contrast; check how trials are defined.

Source encoding under distraction, back-sorted by later memory. Encoding only.
Multiple-object tracking to modulate reactivation, with classifiers. Not a retrieval-success contrast.
